preamble: Depalatalization of the alveolo-palatal affricate [tɕ] to the alveolar affricate [ts]. In Cantonese, the alveolo-palatal sibilants (from the Middle Chinese retroflex and palatal series) merged with the alveolar series in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, so that 張 and 將 are now homophones. In Kashubian, the alveolo-palatals that arose from Proto-Slavic soft t, d, s, z (still ć, dź, ś, ź in Polish) hardened to dental c, dz, s, z, probably before the 17th century (kaszëbienié).

examples.note: Now homophonous with 將, which already had /ts/; Mandarin zhāng has retroflex [ʈʂ]. Williams (1856) already noted that ch and ts were 'constantly confounded'.
Short i after the new dental became ë.
